Andes.question: Río de la Plata and _____ derive their names from the silver of Potosí
Andes.fact: === Mining === The Andes rose to fame for their mineral wealth during the Spanish conquest of South America.  Although Andean Amerindian peoples crafted ceremonial jewelry of gold and other metals, the mineralizations of the Andes were first mined on a large scale after the Spanish arrival.  Potosí in present-day Bolivia and Cerro de Pasco in Peru were among the principal mines of the Spanish Empire in the New World.  Río de la Plata and Argentina derive their names from the silver of Potosí.  Currently, mining in the Andes of Chile and Peru places these countries as the first and second major producers of copper in the world.  Peru also contains the 4th-largest goldmine in the world: the Yanacocha.  The Bolivian Andes principally produce tin, although historically silver mining had a huge impact on the economy of 17th-century Europe
